'''Félix Malu wa Kalenga'''  (September 22, 1936 — April 22, 2011) was a [[Democratic Republic of the Congo|Congolese]] [[emeritus]] [[professor]] of [[Nuclear physics|Nuclear Physics]] and a [[scientist]]. He was a founding member of the [[The World Academy of Sciences|Third World Academy of Science]] (TWAS).<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=Kalenga Felix Malu Wa {{!}} The AAS |url=https://www.aasciences.africa/fellow/kalenga-felix-malu-wa |access-date=2022-11-15 |website=www.aasciences.africa |archive-date=2022-11-15 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221115173831/https://www.aasciences.africa/fellow/kalenga-felix-malu-wa |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref name=":3">{{Cite web |title=Malu Wa Kalenga, Félix |url=https://twas.org/directory/malu-wa-kalenga-felix |access-date=2022-11-15 |website=TWAS |language=en}}</ref> He was a  professor at [[Lovanium University]] and a Dean of the Polytechnic Faculty of the [[University of Kinshasa]]. He was also a commissioner of the general commission for atomic energy (CGEA) in the DRC and a director general of the regional center for nuclear studies in Kinshasa.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Belgique: vibrant hommage rendu au Pr Félix Malu wa Kalenga {{!}} adiac-congo.com : toute l'actualité du Bassin du Congo |url=https://www.adiac-congo.com/content/belgique-vibrant-hommage-rendu-au-pr-felix-malu-wa-kalenga-52277 |access-date=2022-11-15 |website=www.adiac-congo.com}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Malu was born on September 22, 1936, in [[Boma, Democratic Republic of the Congo|Boma, Congo]]. He obtained a BSc in Electrical Engineering and Electronics from Lovanium University in 1962. He obtained his MSc at the [[University of California]], Berkeley, in 1963 and in 1969, he earned his doctorate degree in applied sciences at the  [[Université catholique de Louvain]].<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Félix Malu wa Kalenga |url=https://www.pas.va/en/academicians/deceased/malu.html |access-date=2022-11-15 |website=www.pas.va |language=en}}</ref>

== Career ==
=== Academic career ===
He was a professor at the Faculty of Applied Sciences at the University of Kinshasa, Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC); he became the dean of the institution in 1970 and in 2000 he became an emeritus professor.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=Luc |title=Seated on the shoulders of a giant |url=https://www.afriscitech.com/en/blogs/raissa-malu/972-seated-on-the-shoulders-of-a-giant |access-date=2022-11-15 |website=www.afriscitech.com |language=en-gb |archive-date=2022-11-15 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221115174737/https://www.afriscitech.com/en/blogs/raissa-malu/972-seated-on-the-shoulders-of-a-giant |url-status=dead }}</ref>

=== Scientific career ===
Malu wa Kalenga led construction of the Triga Mark II reactor at the Regional Center for Nuclear Studies in Kinshasa.<ref name=":1" /> From 1965 to 2000 he was a Commissioner at the General Commission for Atomic Energy (CGEA) in the DRC and a Director General of the Kinshasa Regional Center for Nuclear Studies.<ref name=":0" />

== Fellowship and membership ==
He was a founding member of the World Academy of Sciences (TWAS), a member of the board of governors of the [[International Atomic Energy Agency]] (IAEA), Vienna. A board member of the United Nations University, in Tokyo and he was also a member of the OAU Scientific Council, a member of the advisory scientific council of the Theoretical Physics Agency of Trieste, Italy, a member of the scientific advisory board of the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA), Vienna, and a member of the Vatican Pontifical Academy of Sciences for Applied Physics.<ref name=":2" /><ref name=":3" /><ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" />

== Death ==
Malu wa Kalenga died on April 22, 2011.<ref name=":0" />
